paper.title_en: Renormalization-group flow of nucleon--$Δ$ contact interactions with an explicit $Δ$: decoupling and the scale dependence of large-$N_c$ relations
paper.abstract_en: We study the leading-order (LO) contact interactions among nucleons and $Δ$ isobars under a Wilsonian renormalization-group flow with a sharp momentum cutoff, keeping the $Δ$ as an explicit coupled channel, and determine which large-$N_c$ relations among the couplings are invariant under the flow. The two-channel flow with the $ΔΔ$ threshold inside the cutoff range is solved exactly, and the closed channels decouple with relative corrections of order $Λ^2/κ_{ΔΔ}^2$, where $κ_{ΔΔ}=\sqrt{2M_Δ(M_Δ-M_N)}$ is the closed-channel momentum. Applying the $1/N_c$ expansion of the Hartree Hamiltonian to the $N$--$Δ$ system, we find that a generalized time reversal removes all corrections of relative order $1/N_c$, that the LO fixes eleven of the 18 S-wave couplings in terms of seven, and that the exact-SU(4) two-parameter form used in the literature differs from the LO by an operator of relative order $1/N_c^2$ with matrix elements of order one in the $Δ$ channels. The eight spin--isospin flip relations are exact invariants of the flow, also when the central part of one-pion exchange is iterated in the S waves. The eigenchannel relations of the $NN$--$ΔΔ$ sectors hold only at the scale at which they are imposed. Their running is controlled by $κ_{ΔΔ}$, which is of order $N_c^0$, and by a parameter that the $NN$ data do not fix, so that the $1/N_c$ expansion does not remove it. Large-$N_c$ relations between open and closed channels therefore constrain the potential at one scale. The flip relation between the $(S,I)=(3,0)$ and $(0,3)$ channels of $ΔΔ$ scattering predicts equal scattering lengths at LO, which lattice QCD at heavy pion masses can test.
